editorial:
Imagine being a teenager and deciding to spend your time helping other kids who have it even worse than you do. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a young girl who starts working at a center for girls who cannot live with their parents. It starts out as a way for her to do something good, but she quickly finds herself way over her head. The vibe is very emotional and grounded, showing you the raw struggles these girls face every day. You will feel for the main character as she tries to be a hero in a system that does not really want to change.

What really works is how the movie shows the clash between the kids and the adults. The acting feels real, and the drama builds up naturally as she gets into trouble with her boss and her own parents. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you like stories about friendship and fighting for what is right, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the main character realizes that the rules of the center often hurt the girls more than they help them. After a lot of fighting with her supervisor, she manages to create a real bond with the residents. The movie wraps up with a bittersweet feeling. While she cannot fix every single problem, she learns that showing kindness and being a true friend is the most important thing she can offer.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about social issues and teenage growth.
